lesson.menu_desc: A short call with the CFO before the budget review: checking that everybody agrees, finding the surprise before the meeting, and never pushing -- question tags
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 31 -- Before the Big Meeting: checking agreement without pushing
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Patrícia Xavier Lima Iwashita | Lesson 31 -- Before the Big Meeting
lesson.grammar_point: question tags (..., isn't it? / ..., didn't you? / ..., shouldn't we?)

listenings.text: Hi Patrícia, it is Karen. Before the Brightwave budget review, remember the golden rule: the big meeting is not the place for surprises. Nobody should hear a number for the first time there. So book a short call with Victor this week, and send him a one-page pre-read two days before the call. On the call, check that you agree, but do not push. Question tags are perfect for this. You say: the numbers look good, don't they? And then you let him answer. If he says no, great: you found the problem before the meeting, not in it. And please do a dry run with me on Thursday. Fifteen minutes is enough.

Hi Patrícia, it is Daniel. Victor told me about your call. Thank you for looping me in. Two things before the meeting. First, the board likes short answers, so prepare three talking points and no more. Second, they will ask about the outage in August, won't they? I think you should mention it before they do. Say what happened, what you changed, and show them the new alert. If you say it first, it sounds like control. If they ask first, it sounds like a secret. See you on Monday.
